posts.text: Still processing this one. This week, our team competed in the first-ever Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (CNL) Case Competition at Western University, and I’m really proud to share that we placed 1st in our category. Huge shoutout to Ruo-Tong Wong and Kenodh Ekanayake. A few weeks ago we didn’t know each other at all, and in a short time we built a team that genuinely pushed one another to think more critically, communicate clearly, and stay composed when things got intense. University is cooked. We got our Calc 2 midterm back and 60% of people basically failed. Unlike high school where you could cram the chapters the day before, university has been a big learning curve. The grade distribution was honestly the most interesting part. Most of the class was packed in the middle, with only a few people scoring above 75%. That graph tells the story perfectly. You don’t really notice how fast things add up until everything’s on one schedule. Finishing the first week and looking at my schedule made that pretty clear. Not in an overwhelming way, just a reminder that this semester is going to demand consistency, focus, and actually showing up each day. What stood out to me this week wasn’t any single class or assignment, but how quickly the pace picks up once things start.
